narrative:
The model determined that you have a 64% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability exceeds the school's acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your academic record. Your third-year class ranking had the strongest influence and worked in your favor: placing in the top decile (9th) is substantially better than the average 5.8 decile seen among accepted students, and this strong performance pulled the prediction toward passing. However, two other factors pushed harder in the opposite direction. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.0 is noticeably below the 3.23 average of accepted applicants and increased the estimated risk of failure. Your first-year class ranking (6th decile) also contributed to raising the predicted failure risk, though to a lesser extent.

Taken together, the model concluded that the combination of your undergraduate grades and earlier law-school performance outweighed the benefit of your excellent third-year ranking, resulting in a failure probability too high for admission.

You should focus on strengthening the areas the model flagged. Retaking courses to raise your undergraduate GPA, or gaining additional academic experience that demonstrates sustained high performance, would most directly address the factors that worked against you. Consider reapplying once those improvements are reflected in your record.
